title: Animals of the Jungle
description: Four recordings about jungle animals: a film, a talk about elephants, a zoo keeper and a trip message.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · A wildlife film
parts.intro: You will hear Sam and Linh watching a film about the jungle.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Sam, look at that tiger! It's walking along the river.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: It's beautiful, but I'm a little scared. Tigers are very big and strong.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Don't worry, we're only watching a film. My favourite animals are the monkeys, though. Look at the baby on its mother's back.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: Yes, and the parrots are great, too. They're red and blue, and they can say words.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Actually, in the jungle they just make loud noises. People teach them words at home.

script.speaker: Sam
script.text: I didn't know that. Do you think there are snakes?

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Yes, a few. But the film says most snakes are shy and stay away from people.

parts.title: Part 2 · A talk about elephants
parts.intro: You will hear Dr Mai giving a short talk about elephants.

script.speaker: Dr Mai
script.text: Today I'm going to tell you about elephants. They are the biggest animals that live on land.

script.speaker: Dr Mai
script.text: An elephant eats up to two hundred kilos of food every day. It eats grass, leaves and fruit, and it drinks a lot of water, too.

script.speaker: Dr Mai
script.text: Surprisingly, elephants only sleep for about four hours each night. They sleep standing up.

script.speaker: Dr Mai
script.text: Elephants live in family groups. The oldest female is the leader, and the babies stay close to their mothers for many years.

script.speaker: Dr Mai
script.text: They talk to each other with loud sounds through their trunks. Some sounds are so low that people can't hear them. Elephants are clever and gentle, and we must protect them.

parts.title: Part 3 · Talking to a zoo keeper
parts.intro: You will hear Nam asking a zoo keeper, Ms Jane, about some jungle animals.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Excuse me, Ms Jane. Why is that animal in the tree so still?

script.speaker: Ms Jane
script.text: That's a sloth. It moves very slowly, so it uses very little energy. It even sleeps hanging upside down.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Wow! And what are those small green animals on the leaves?

script.speaker: Ms Jane
script.text: They're tree frogs. Their skin is bright, and some are poisonous, so please don't touch them. They come out at night.

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Do they eat flies?

script.speaker: Ms Jane
script.text: Yes, flies and other small insects. Now come with me. It's time to feed the monkeys. Would you like to help?

script.speaker: Nam
script.text: Yes, please! What do they eat?

script.speaker: Ms Jane
script.text: Bananas, nuts and fruit. But we never give them sweets, because sugar is bad for them.

parts.title: Part 4 · A message about a jungle trip
parts.intro: You will hear a phone message from a guide, Mr Green.

script.speaker: Mr Green
script.text: Hello, this is Mr Green, your guide for the jungle trip. I'm calling to give you some information.

script.speaker: Mr Green
script.text: We leave very early, at six o'clock, because the birds sing best at dawn. The walk through the forest takes three hours.

script.speaker: Mr Green
script.text: Please wear long trousers and a hat, and bring some water. You will also need insect spray, because there are lots of mosquitoes.

script.speaker: Mr Green
script.text: We will see parrots and, if we are lucky, a family of monkeys. Please don't feed the monkeys, and keep quiet near the animals.

script.speaker: Mr Green
script.text: After the walk, we will have lunch by the river. Call me if you have any questions. Goodbye!
